bullets.title: Semis/AI broad rally: sector up 4%+ on oversold reversal, echoes Dec 2018 bottom
bullets.body: SOXX ETF +4.04% premarket with 40+ semiconductor names gaining 3-10%; LITE +7.8%, COHR +7.5%, ANET +4.3%, SHOP +4.3%, DELL +4.3%. Analyst notes Wednesday's 8% intraday reversal from lows resembles the Dec 2018 inflection — but memory stocks (MU, SNDK) lagging badly, with MU down 15% and SNDK down 24% over 5 days despite premarket bounces, signaling zero real buyer conviction in that sub-segment.

bullets.title: NVDA: bullish admin support narrative vs. China Blackwell smuggling risk ahead of Jensen testimony
bullets.body: Roth Capital frames Jensen Huang's upcoming Congressional testimony as a net positive, calling this a 'Jensen 2.0' era with admin support; Trump positioned as NVDA-friendly. However, reports of Blackwell chips found in a Shanghai data center triggered softness in S&P futures at 6:44am ET, and a GPU investigation into SE Asia/Megaspeed distribution is expected to surface surprises. ASML also cited at risk if Dutch government resists U.S. Match Act export controls (China is 23% of ASML systems revenue).

bullets.title: OKTA Q3 preview: consensus $816M rev/$0.93 EPS; 20-for-20 beat rate, options imply ~16% move
bullets.body: OKTA Q3 consensus sits at $816M revenue vs. guidance midpoint $815M and EPS $0.93 vs. guidance $0.92-$0.94; stock is +50% since late August. OKTA has beaten both revenue and EPS consensus in all 20 of the last 20 quarters. Near-term options imply a ~16.2% post-earnings move.

bullets.title: NTSK: KeyBanc raises PT to $30 on strong VAR checks; S flagged as flat demand despite cheap valuation
bullets.body: KeyBanc VAR channel checks for NTSK were uniformly positive — four U.S. VARs cited F100 wins and improved GTM execution; expect F3Q ARR beat of ~$7M at ~$954M (27% y/y) with NNARR accelerating to 18% y/y. NTSK trades at 11.3x CY27 revenue vs. security sector avg 9.8x. SentinelOne (S) checks were below plan with no demand inflection; large F4Q deal shows customer consolidating onto CrowdStrike; S trades at just 5.9x revenue but fundamentals not yet inflecting.

bullets.title: WDAY: Hedgeye flags decelerating growth — RPO missed by $1.1B, subscription margins at multi-year low
bullets.body: WDAY subscription revenue growth slowed to ~11.5% in H2 vs. 14.1% H1, with Q4 guided at +10%. Total RPO grew just +6.1% to $27.5B, $1.1B below Street estimates, marking 13 consecutive quarters of RPO growth deceleration. AI ARR exceeded $750M (>130% YoY) but is substituting for core HR/finance spend rather than adding incremental growth; subscription gross margin hit its lowest level since Q4 FY23.

bullets.title: PLTR: $300M Poland defense AI deal signed
bullets.body: Palantir signed a $300M defense AI contract with Poland, cited as a catalyst driving the stock +3% in premarket trading Friday.

bullets.title: MRVL, CRM, SNOW: earnings next week — key upcoming catalysts
bullets.body: MRVL reports after close Tuesday, with CRM and SNOW both reporting after close Wednesday. These are flagged as key positioning events into next week alongside the AMZN re:Invent keynote Tuesday.

bullets.title: TSEM: Mizuho hosts mgmt call Dec 3; Outperform/$235 PT on SiPho ramp and 300mm adoption
bullets.body: Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh maintains Outperform on TSEM with $235 PT. Dec 3 group call will cover SiPho supply constraints, GFS/STM competitive dynamics, NPO ramps in 2027, and CPO contemplated for 2029/30. Japan capacity expansion and margin progression as 300mm scales are also on the agenda.

bullets.title: SHOP: +4.3-4.5% in premarket on broad risk-on; no stock-specific catalyst
bullets.body: Shopify is up 4.3-4.5% across both U.S. and Canadian listings in premarket/morning trading, moving with the broad tech/AI risk-on rally rather than any company-specific news.

bullets.title: PINS: Unusual options activity — 237% above 30-day avg, bullish P/C ratio of 2.15
bullets.body: Pinterest saw 45,222 option contracts vs. a 30-day average of 19,076, a 237% spike, with a put/call ratio of 2.15 indicating bullish positioning. No specific catalyst identified beyond broad market momentum.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone Duo softening in China — 21% resale price decline, $225 discounts
bullets.body: iPhone Duo is selling at $225 discounts in China with a ~21% resale price decline, signaling meaningful demand softening in that market. No rating change or PT update provided.

bullets.title: CSCO: OpenAI 'Shirudo' open-source security partnership launched
bullets.body: Cisco and OpenAI jointly launched Shirudo, an open-source project designed to protect infrastructure against AI-driven cyberattacks. No financial guidance was updated in connection with the announcement.

bullets.title: SPOT: Roth Capital quantifies pricing power and churn risk vs. AMZN/AAPL
bullets.body: Roth Capital published a subscriber survey examining whether Spotify can sustain price increases without accelerating churn, measuring price tolerance and payment behavior across SPOT, AMZN Music, and AAPL Music. Specific findings not yet disclosed but framed as a key positioning study for the streaming space.

bullets.title: DIS, OMC hit 52-week highs — DIS +22.9% YTD, OMC +25.6% YTD
bullets.body: DIS reached $127.00 (+1.1% on the day, +22.9% 52-week) and OMC hit $91.50 (+0.9%, +25.6% 52-week) on the morning scan of new 52-week highs across 77 names.

bullets.title: HUT, WULF, IREN, BTDR: Crypto miners up 3-6%+ on broad risk-on rally
bullets.body: Bitcoin miner names HUT (+3.6% on TSX), WULF, IREN, and BTDR are all trading higher in premarket as part of the broad AI/risk-on tape. No stock-specific catalysts cited.

bullets.title: SMR, OKLO: Nuclear names +6% on data center power demand narrative
bullets.body: SMR is up ~6% in premarket trading on continued nuclear reactor demand from data center power requirements; OKLO also cited as moving higher with the broader nuclear/data center theme.

bullets.title: AAOI, NBIS: Optical/AI infra names lead premarket — AAOI +9.5-10%, NBIS +6%
bullets.body: AAOI surged 9.5-10% and NBIS gained 6% in premarket trading, among the strongest movers in the AI infrastructure/optical interconnect space on the broad risk-on reversal.

bullets.title: Quant: Semi/hardware momentum baskets collapsed -35%/-14% MTD; EPS-Mo/short-Price-Mo swap up 20% YTD
bullets.body: 22V quant notes Tech Hardware and Semis price-momentum baskets fell -35.1% and -14.4% MTD respectively, accounting for -4.7pp of the S&P 1500's -5.3% November decline. Short-term volatility in Price Momentum hit 93rd percentile. Recommended long-EPS Momentum / short-Price Momentum swap is up 20.2% since late-June launch; they recommend blending Value and Momentum factors going forward.

bullets.title: Macro: S&P bounce expected but limited — PCE at 3.8%, Fed stays hawkish, range cap ~7600
bullets.body: 22V sees Q3 GDP revised to 4.3% and strong October retail sales supporting EPS, but October PCE at 3.8% YoY and nominal GDP at 6.3% keep the Fed firmly hawkish. A rally above ~7,600 on the S&P would tighten financial conditions via higher UST yields, limiting upside. Core PCE needs to fall 21bp/month to hit the Fed's 2027 target — an unlikely near-term path.
